title: Zhalm forest sound-network encounter
hypothesis: Movement noise feeding a visible root-sensor network creates legible stealth pressure: a player can read the network's alert state from node pulses alone, choose speed to manage noise, and de-escalate a triggered guardian by staying quiet — before any real AI, art or audio exists.
success_signals: A first-time player can explain the guardian's three alert levels purely from node and guardian visuals.
Sprinting near a sensor reliably triggers a visible pulse cascade and an investigation of the noise position.
Walking slowly past the same sensor does not trigger the cascade at default tunables.
Staying quiet and distant de-escalates a chase back to calm, and the grove heart is reachable through deliberate routing.
kill_criteria: Players cannot tell suspicious from alerted no matter how tunables are set (readability failure).
The dominant strategy is pure sprinting because noise pressure never matters (mechanic failure).
Network propagation cost makes the scene unplayable at 7 nodes (feasibility failure).
reset_strategy: Teleport the player to spawn with zeroed velocity, clear all node energy and stimulation, return the guardian to its den in calm state, and reset win/catch counters. Deterministic, no backend state.
